supplex: supplex, supplicis — suppliant, begging humbly (nom. sg.)
syrtibus: Syrtis, -is (f.) — Syrtis, sandbank, the shoals off north Africa (abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tanti: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. pl.; n. gen. sg.)
tanto: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m./n. abl. sg.)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tecti: tectum, -ī (n.) — roof, house (gen. sg.) · also tectus, -a, -um — sheltered, covered; tegō perf. pass. part. (m. nom. pl.: tectī silvīs)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
templa: templum, -ī (n.) — temple, sanctuary, sacred precinct (acc./nom. pl.)
tempus: tempus, -oris (n.) — time, season, hour (nom. sg.) · also n. acc. sg. (tempus inane peto)
tenus: tenus (prep. + abl., placed after its noun) — as far as, up to
terrae: terra, -ae (f.) — earth, land, country (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
thalami: thalamus, -ī (m.) — bedchamber, marriage-chamber (nom. pl.; also gen. sg.)
thybrim: Thybris, -idis (m.) — the Tiber (acc. sg., Greek form in -im)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
totidem: totidem (indecl. adj.) — just as many, the same number
troiae: Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (gen. sg.) · also dat. sg., for Troy (sīc fāta ferēbant)
troiana: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tuas: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. acc. pl.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turbata: turbō, -āre — to disturb, throw into confusion (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
unus: ūnus, -a, -um — one, alone, a single (m. nom. sg.)
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
venis: veniō, venīre, vēnī, ventum — to come (2nd sg. pres.) · also vēna, -ae (f.) — vein, blood-vessel (abl. pl.: volnus alit venis)
venisse: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (perf. inf.)
ventum: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (perf. pass. part., n. sg., in impersonal ventum est, they came) · also ventus, -ī (m.) — wind (acc. sg.: in ventum, 'into the wind')
videri: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see; pass. to be seen, seem (pres. pass. inf.)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl. (festīnāte, virī)
vocat: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd sg. pres.)
voces: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, utterance (acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
voltus: vultus (voltus), -ūs (m.) — face, look, expression (nom. sg.; acc. pl.) · also nom. pl. (haerent … voltus)
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.) · also voc. pl. (vōs, aetērnī ignēs)
vota: vōtum, -ī (n.) — vow, promise to a god, prayer (acc./nom. pl.)
xanthus: Xanthus, -ī (m.) — Xanthus, river of Troy (nom. sg.)
